panels.title: Queue Depth
panels.description: Steps held in each replica's in-memory worker cache.

Parked steps the defense-in-depth wedge sweep had to recover, by park type (subgraph/breaker). Should always be zero in steady state - a nonzero value means a park release was lost and a latent bug let a step wedge.
panels.title: Steps Unwedged

panels.description: Running flows the orphan sweep found stranded - every step terminal with no successor. Detection only, not recovery: a nonzero value is a latent bug.
panels.title: Flows Orphaned

panels.description: Steps terminalized because their outcome could not be stored while the database was reachable. A nonzero value is a latent bug.
panels.title: Step Write Failures

panels.description: In-place retries of a step's persistence write after a database blip. The task is not re-executed, so this is a database-health signal, not duplicated work.
panels.title: Step Write Retries
Pending Steps by Priority
panels.description: Due pending steps per priority band. Cluster-wide: every replica queries the same shared databases and reports the same number, so this aggregates with max, not sum.

panels.title: Pending Backlog vs Local Cache (refiller throughput)
panels.description: The shared backlog (cluster-wide, aggregated with max) against this fleet's local worker caches (per-replica, summed). Cache tracking the backlog means selection is keeping up.

panels.title: Steps Executed by Shard
panels.description: Per-shard dispatch throughput. Selection, the connection pool and the work split are all per shard, so a fleet-wide total hides one shard falling behind. There is deliberately no per-fairness-key metric: that label would be unbounded cardinality, so fairness and priority are aggregate-only.
Replicas each engine sees holding connections to that shard - the divisor its connection pool is sized by. It should settle at the intended replica count.
panels.title: Replicas per Shard

panels.description: Time since that shard's peer registry was last read successfully. Zero when healthy; a rising value means pool sizing is working off a stale replica count.
panels.title: Peer Registry Blind Time

panels.description: Observed changes in a shard's replica count. Flat in a settled fleet by construction, so continued movement outside a deploy means replicas are churning.
panels.title: Fleet Churn

panels.description: Where new flows landed. Placement is weighted by each shard's declared VirtualCPUs, so a skew that does not match the configured capacities means work is not spread as intended.
panels.title: Flows Placed by Shard

panels.description: Steps selected from outside this replica's own share of the work, because the replica owning that share was not serving it. Zero in a healthy fleet by construction; a sustained rate names a peer that is alive but not dispatching.
panels.title: Steps Stolen by Shard

panels.description: Worker goroutines that exist across the fleet. The pool grows on demand and retires mostly idle workers, never below the connection-derived floor. Rising and settling back is that working; wide oscillation at steady load is not.
panels.title: Workers Resident

panels.description: Worker goroutines inside a database phase right now, which is what sets connection-pool pressure. `enter` is dispatch up to the task call, `exit` is the task call to the end of the step; they are separate populations. Wrap in max_over_time for the peak a phase actually reached rather than whatever the scrape caught.
panels.title: Workers Inside a Database Phase

panels.description: Wall clock a worker spent inside a database phase - its true residence, which neither the turn waits (the queue in front of each call) nor the sum of query times (which misses connection wait and the Go-side work between them) can supply.
panels.title: Database Phase Residence 99%ile

panels.description: Read as a pair. Turns are a fixed multiple of the connection pool, so `available` is how much admission is unspoken for and a sustained zero means the shard's connections are the binding constraint. `waiting` has no ceiling, so it is the one that shows how deep the queue has become rather than merely that it is full.
panels.title: Turnstile Turns: Available vs Waiting

panels.description: `gate` is the wait for a worker's first turn, taken before it picks a step up - the queue in front of dispatch, and the only wait a worker holds no work through. `record` is the wait for the turn that stores a finished step; work that has already run presents an older claim than anything admitted while it ran, so a sustained wait there means the shard's connections are busy with work at least as old, not that completions are queued behind dispatch.
panels.title: Turnstile Wait 99%ile: Gate vs Record

panels.description: Cached candidates replaced before a worker picked them up, over candidates selected. Each pass replaces the cache wholesale, so this is cost and never lost work - the steps stay pending and are re-selected. Approaching 1 means selection is running far ahead of what the workers consume and most of its database round trips are thrown away; near 0 means selection is the slower half.
panels.title: Selection Waste Ratio

panels.description: How long ago the stalest shard still counted in this replica's selection last reported.
panels.title: Refill Tally Age

panels.description: Read `preempted` against `lost`. Preempted candidates were skipped before any claim because a sibling worker on this replica already had one in flight - round trips saved. Lost ones were claimed and then lost the CAS to a peer - round trips wasted. A healthy engine converts what would have been lost into preempted. `offered` steps arrived by the doorbell rather than a scan.
panels.title: Claim Outcomes

panels.description: Selection queries every shard concurrently and proceeds only when the last one answers, so one shard's tail dragging while the others stay flat bounds dispatch for the whole replica.
panels.title: Refill Query 99%ile by Shard

panels.description: The two queries a selection pass runs. A tail on band_keys alone, intermittent and on an unchanged backlog, points at the query planner rather than load - on PostgreSQL stale table statistics can flip it between an index scan and a sequential scan. ANALYZE on dwarf_steps, or more aggressive autovacuum for it, is the fix.
panels.title: Refill Query 99%ile by Phase

panels.description: State this fleet is holding across host calls, and the mean a single task carries. Read the mean, not the total: a few tasks each carrying a large document and a wide fan-out of tasks each carrying a little produce the same total but call for different fixes - narrowing what the workflow carries, versus the fan-out width. Measured as the JSON the state was built from, so against your heap it gives the expansion factor.
panels.title: In-Flight State: Bytes and Mean per Task

panels.description: Tasks currently inside a task call - the denominator of the mean beside it. A task holds no database connection while it runs, so the worker pool grows freely for long tasks and held state times pool size is a memory ceiling the resident-worker count cannot show alone.
panels.title: In-Flight Tasks

panels.description: Payload bytes written to step rows on the execution path.
panels.title: State Bytes Written by Column

panels.description: Payload bytes read from step rows on the execution path.
panels.title: State Bytes Read by Column
